Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Bangladesh's second innings! The Zimbabwe players make their way out to the middle, followed by Saif Hassan and Shadman Islam. Blessing Muzarabani will start with the ball.

Bangladesh were brilliant with the ball on Day 3! They started off slowly, picking just a wicket in the first session but since the second session, they were superb. Mehidy Hasan led with the ball with a 5-fer and Shakib Al Hasan took a 4-wicket haul. Even the seamers were terrific and they hold all the cards at the moment. They will look to bat till Stumps without hiccups and then take the game forward. Join us in a while.

Zimbabwe would be disappointed! They started off so well, with Takudzwanashe Kaitano and Milton Shumba doing a very good job. Brendan Taylor played a brilliant innings but he needed to continue. After he fell, they collapsed and lost wickets regular intervals. Kaitano missed out on a century while there was nothing else from the others. Overall, a disappointing performance.

Mehidy Hasan, take a bow! What a performance! He has been a different bowler in 2021 and is continuing his form. His 5-fer has helped them get a lead of 192 runs which is a very good read on this wicket. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, will be disappointed as they were in a good position at the start of the day but they have faltered big time.

OUT! CAUGHT! That is the end. Shakib Al Hasan gets his fourth wicket. Zimbabwe's struggles continues post-Lunch. The spinners were all over the Zimbabwean tail. Serves it full and on off. Richard Ngarava prods and looks to defend it. The ball takes the outside edge and flies to the man at first slip. Najmul Hossain Shanto grabs the ball in the second attempt to end things for the hosts. Richard Ngarava becomes the fourth batsman today to get dismissed on a duck. ZIMBABWE END THEIR INNINGS AT 276 for 10.
Commentary.Howout: c Najmul Hossain Shanto b Shakib Al Hasan

Welcome back for the final session of Day 3! The Bangladesh players make their way out to the middle, followed by Takudzwanashe Kaitano and Regis Chakabva. Shakib Al Hasan will start with the ball after the Tea break. 35 overs remaining in the day.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Oh yes, the Zimbabwe side was a part of a collapse as they lost 3 wickets in the second session, not how they envisioned it. Kaitano remains to be a constant on one side of the pitch but he sees his partners rattle throughout. He has Chakabva now alongside him, and they would look to see off the day to keep Zimbabwe in this game. The final session of Day 3 begins at 2.30 pm local (1230 GMT). Do join us then.

We are back for the second session! The Bangladesh players stride out to the middle, followed by Takudzwanashe Kaitano and Dion Myers. Shakib Al Hasan will start with the ball after Lunch.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

Bangladesh's bowling was decent! The pacers were really good as they bowled probing lines and lengths. They beat the bat quite a few times but were unlucky not to find a wicket. The spinners have not had the same impact but they are the ones in the wickets column. Mehidy Hasan was looking good but Shakib Al Hasan needs to put his hand up. They will look to come back and get quick wickets and push Zimbabwe on the back foot. The second session will begin at 12.10 pm local (1010 GMT). Do join us then.

Day 3 for Zimbabwe began with a good stand between Kaitano and Taylor. They looked solid in the middle, as they saw out more than an hour of the day with ease. It was then an attacking attempt of Taylor that took him out. He was gutted with his approach, his side would have been in a better position with him in the middle till lunch. Now it is on the two debutants in the middle to take their team to safer shores.

A very good session for Zimbabwe! Yes, they did lose a wicket of Brendan Taylor but Kaitano has played really well and is looking really solid. Dion Myers has come out and has looked confident but their job is not done yet and they need to continue. Bangladesh, on the other hand, need to continue taking wickets. Overall, a very engrossing session.

Pitch report - Tino Mawoyo says that the pitch has continued to improve. Adds that on a length, the grass is drying out and the greenness is going away and the assistance won't be there on Day 3. Tells that this will be a good batting surface on Day 3 and probably Day 4. States that this is going to dry out and it might cause some problems to the right-handed batsmen.

Takudzwanashe Kaitano is there for a chat.. He says that he is very pleased. Adds that Mahmudullah and Taskin played really well. Goes onto say that they will try hard to reach Bangladesh's score. Hello and a warm welcome to the third day's play between Zimbabwe and Bangladesh. Bangladesh owned Day 2 courtesy a record stand between Mahmudullah and Taskin Ahmed. They helped Bangladesh reach 468 but they would have expected to take some quick wickets but Zimbabwe showed great resolve with the bat. Takudzwanashe Kaitano, the debutant is looking in good touch while Brendan Taylor is playing positive cricket. They will look to continue and help Zimbabwe reach closer to Bangladesh's score. Join us in a while.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...
Right then! That is all we have from Day 2. The action continues on 9th July as Day 3 action is set to begin at 0930 Local (0730 GMT). Do join us for that! Till then, goodbye and cheers!

Earlier in the day, Mahmudullah and Taskin Ahmed did all the damage and forged a 191 run partnership to drag Bangladesh out of the danger as they were 294 for 8 at one stage. Their partnership helped Bangladesh add crucial runs to the total score. Zimbabwe bowlers allowed to wag the tail a bit too much as Taskin fell to Shumba after scoring 75 runs doing all the damage. Mahmudullah continued to hang in the middle and brought up his 150. Ebadot Hossain couldn't support him though and fell to Muzarabani to fold Bangladesh's innings for 468.

A patient and a hard-fought innings by Zimbabwe. They have an uphill task on their shoulders to climb the mountain of 468 runs and then extend their lead. The openers for Zimbabwe started well as they scored runs patiently but kept the scoreboard ticking. Milton Shumba and Takudzwanashe Kaitano did well to leave the deliveries that were outside off or any of that sort. Both the batsmen kept the runs flowing in with singles and doubles, knocking a few boundaries on loose deliveries. The batters also stitched a partnership of 61 runs before Milton Shumba departed right after drinks break for a well-fought 41. Brendon Taylor then came in and kept scoring at pace while Kaitano didn't look in a hurry and worked around him. The duo added 53 runs to the total and will look to continue to do the job tomorrow. For Bangladesh, their bowlers did well and not allowed the runs to come freely. Freebies were also not offered and they managed to keep the pressure though they were unsuccessful in finding wickets. Shakib Al Hasan was the only bowler to get the solitary wicket of Shumba. They will now look to wrap things up tomorrow and come out to bat again to put on a huge lead onto them.

DRINKS! Zimbabwe are off to a steady start after Bangladesh's mammoth 468. The good thing is that they haven't lost a single wicket yet. Milton Shumba and Takudzwanashe Kaitano should continue to keep the scoreboard ticking. Bangladesh bowlers have bowled well and have not allowed the runs to come easy. They have gone past the outside edge on a few occasions and will look to break this stand as early as possible.
Fractionally short, on middle. Shumba flicks it off the back foot to mid-wicket to keep the strike.
FOUR! Connects well! Another loopy ball, on the pads. Shumba paddle sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
FOUR! Good shot! Angles this on the pads. Shumba paddle sweeps it past the short fine leg for a boundary.

Flatter delivery on middle and leg, turning away, Shumba looks to defend but misses. The ball gets hit on the pads. Shakib Al Hasan pleads for LBW but nothing from the umpire. It was probably going down the leg side.
